- **⚠⚠ I REPORTED "ZERO CALLS IN THE WINDOW" FOR A REP WITH 141 CALLS, AND ALMOST FILED IT AS THE FAULT.** The only thing that caught it was the shared computation returning 25 prospects for the same rep and window — **a contradiction between two readings of the same data.**
- **THE RULE, already on file and worth restating because it recurred: an implausible empty result is a statement about the instrument.** Check `error` on every call, and be specific about which fields are COLUMNS versus fields the API derives.

### [H657] ⚠ SCORE → COLOUR: A COLOUR THAT CANNOT VARY SHOULD NOT BE A COLOUR (proposed 2026-09-01)
Three instances of one defect: **score badges** (52/100 in the same green as 75/100), **the amber section bars** (all five identical regardless of score), **the objection category** (green while naming the WEAKEST area).
- **ONE RULE: a score is coloured only when it crosses a band, using the product's existing `--good` / `--mid` / `--bad`.** 75 green, 52 amber, sub-40 red.
- **⚠ THE COROLLARY IS WHAT FIXES THE OTHER TWO: if the colour is identical at every value, it encodes nothing and should be neutral.** The WEAKEST/STRONGEST chips already carry the meaning.
- **⚠ ONE EXCEPTION, ALREADY RULED: `.review-why` is an OUTCOME, not a score**, and its colour is correct.

### [H658] ⚠⚠⚠ A NEW RULING THAT REVERSES AN OLD ONE MUST BE SHOWN THE OLD ONE — CLOSING %'s DENOMINATOR (2026-09-01, NOT CHANGED)
**Justin ruled today: *"CLOSING % IS BASED ON CALLS TAKEN IN THE SELECTED DATE RANGE. Calls taken — not prospects."* That is the OPPOSITE of a ruling he made on 2026-08-03, in his own words:**
> *"if 1 prospect takes 3 calls to close that SHOULDN'T count as 3 calls, it's 1 prospect getting closed — if it's multiple follow ups it doesn't matter."*
- **⚠⚠ THE SHIPPED PROSPECTS DENOMINATOR IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT — IT IS WHAT THAT RULING ASKED FOR**, and it shipped as `fetchProspectCloseRates`. **NOT CHANGED**, because a reversal should be deliberate rather than by implication.
- **MEASURED BOTH WAYS BEFORE REPORTING, and they barely differ — 0 to 5 points across eight reps.** Which corroborates the August note: *"per-prospect 40% vs per-call 39% — grouping is NOT what fixed the close rate."*
- **⚠ THE LEGACY `close_rate` IS NOT A THIRD OPTION**: `close_won / close_decided` drops every OPEN call from the denominator — the "decided-only" formula the August ruling explicitly superseded. Rendered nowhere; delete it whichever way this lands.
- **⚠ ONE REAL ARGUMENT FOR CALLS, worth recording either way: under a calls denominator the 355 unreviewed merges stop mattering entirely**, because calls are not grouped. Today each missed merge costs ~0.9 points.
- **THE GENERAL RULE: before implementing a ruling that changes a definition, GREP THIS FILE FOR THE PREVIOUS RULING ON THAT DEFINITION.** A architect restating something in new words is not always aware they are reversing themselves, and the reversal is invisible unless someone puts the two sentences side by side.

### [H659] ⚠⚠ THE WINDOW IS PART OF THE DEFINITION — 7 DAYS vs 30 MADE ONE REP READ 0% AND 16% (fixed 2026-09-01)
**Godwin read 0% (0/25) on the team page and 16% (16/98) on the personal dashboard. Both correct.** The team pages defaulted to 7 days, the personal one to 30.
- **⚠ CLOSING RATE IS A LOW-FREQUENCY METRIC.** A rep closes a handful a month, so a seven-day rate is frequently zero for someone doing fine — **and it reads as a verdict.**

A closing rate makes no comparison. It is a COUNT OF WHAT HAPPENED.** 0 of 25 is not an unmeasurable estimate; it is a fact about twenty-five prospects.

### [H666] ✅ STANDING RULE (Justin, 2026-09-02): A GUARD ON MONEY, ACCESS OR SCOPE EXECUTES THE ROUTE AND ASSERTS THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IS PROVEN BY TWO PLANTS

- **The subtle case:** a sibling test that executes the gate FUNCTION, the classifier, or the epoch state still tests the helper, not the route. "Executes something" is not "executes the thing."

The same failure shape as H267 one level up: not a missing measurement but a measurement of the wrong document. Fix (`b622106`): the guard renders each placement under the view that hosts it, inside the ancestor chain the page builds (`main.page > div > div.section.fade-in > .rep-card-list`, and the `.dash-grid > .dash-card` slot under `team-dashboard`) — it FAILED on the unfixed stylesheet with the exact live values, and passes after `.rep-card` was removed from the row-rule's selector list. The old ruling is written beside the new one in the stylesheet (a reversal shown its predecessor, H658). **Rule: a rendered guard must render under the host's `data-view`/class attributes and ancestor chain, read from the live DOM — never under a bare body.**

The nearest by glyph widths is Saira 600 at 125% (mean |Δwidth| 0.048 cap, stem within 0.006) — and it is still not the face: in Saira the **C is 13% narrower than the U** (asset: identical, 67/67/67 for C/U/T); Saira's **S overshoots by 3%** (asset: 0); Saira's **M is 1.20 cap** wide (asset 1.10); and on the page the asset's S has a **straight diagonal spine with flat, squared terminals**, the C and U are squared, the **M's vertex stops mid-height** and the **Y meets a straight stem** — a wide, squared geometric display face (the Orbitron / Michroma / Audiowide family of forms), where Saira's S curves, its M vertex reaches the baseline and its terminals are angled. Pictures 05–10 in `~/Desktop/scan-reports/wordmark/`: the asset zoomed beside Saira 600/700 at 125% at the same cap height, and the nav row at 22px where the drawn Saira version visibly does not survive beside the asset — the fail case the block named. **The wordmark predates the Saira rollout; the face it was set in is not the deleted Archivo either** (Archivo is a grotesque with round forms). **The face is not in the repo and is not on this machine — an asset question for Justin: which face, or the original artwork.**

### [H696] ✅ THE BACKGROUND TOGGLE REDESIGN (2026-09-03) — A SLIDING TOGGLE TO THE RIGHT OF My Account, THE MESH GLYPH RIDING THE KNOB, NO TEXT LABEL
- **Justin's rulings, live:** placement B — to the right of My Account, at the far edge ("puts it more out of the way"); a real toggle whose KNOB MOVES, never a square that changes colour; the track stays black; a small mesh glyph rides the knob — Scout green when the artwork is ON, grey when OFF; the text label goes — the glyph is what tells a user what it controls; one object, never two.
- **What it inherits and keeps:** the 1px white edge in BOTH states (`--edge-white`, the product's one white — the track's edge never appears or disappears); the control's own box never changes between states (only the knob moves inside it); the Account checkbox stays the same setting's second door through the one setter (executed both ways in the guard, and clicked live both ways); `role="switch"`, `aria-checked`, the accessible name "Background artwork" (now the ONLY name a screen reader has), the accent focus ring.
- **Built:** a 44×24 black pill track (a pill is a shape), an 18px knob on `--bg-field` with 20px of travel, and the glyph as a CSS `mask-image` of the repo's own vector (`/scout-glyph.svg`) so its colour is CSS — `--accent` on, `--text` dimmed off. No second copy of the path; no new lattice drawn. Rendered guard: the real nav under the real stylesheet with both vectors inlined, in both states — edge, black track, pill radius, knob travel ≥ 16px, glyph colours and ≥15px height, no text, identical box, and the bar / wordmark / My Account rects identical between states. Seven plants fail (a conditional edge, a coloured track, a frozen knob, a green off-glyph, a growing box, a label creeping back, the setter's sync removed).
- **The look-at-it question — does the glyph read at knob size?** At device pixels (a 36px knob on retina) the ON state reads as the mark: green arcs and dots on the dark knob, small but recognisably the glyph. The OFF state at `.45` opacity read as a faint ghost; lifted to `.55` after looking (H697). The three rings do crowd at 16px, as the favicon measurement said; on the knob the position carries the state and the glyph carries the identity. It is not a smudge; it is small. Pictures in `~/Desktop/scan-reports/toggle/`.

### [H697] 🐛 THE TOP BAR HAD SILENTLY GROWN TO 55px (2026-09-03) — CAUGHT MEASURING THE TOGGLE, FIXED BY DECLARING THE 51
- The bar was 14px padding + a 22px line + 14px + a 1px border = 51, and the rail's top, the ground's min-height and the sidebar's max-height are all derived from that 51 (H700). **The vector wordmark at 25.71px (H695) grew the line box, so the bar rendered 55px — for one block, unnoticed, because the IMAGE was measured (164.8 × 25.7, cap 12.13) and the BAR was not.** Found only because the toggle's guard re-measured the bar and the live number was 55.
- **Fix:** `.top-bar { height: 51px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 0 32px }` — the number is a fact the contents cannot move; `align-items: center` places the 25.71px wordmark and the 24px track inside it. **Both rendered guards pin the bar at 51** (the wordmark's and the toggle's), and the toggle's guard also asserts the track fits with ≥2px on both sides — a plant at 40px survived (it fits, with 5px each side — not a defect), a plant at 52px fails. **Rule: when a surface's height is derived elsewhere, guard the SURFACE, not the thing you put in it.**

### [H698] 🔎 AUTO-MARKING NON-SALES CALLS — RECON (2026-09-03). THE CONTROL SET, JUSTIN'S TWO CAVEATS FOUND IN THE CORPUS, THE GRADER ALREADY SAYING THE VERDICT IN PROSE, AND THE CLOSER SELF-MARKS THAT REMOVE REAL CALLS
- **The control set:** 275 marks; 190 automatic (181 `source_disconnected`, 9 `compromised_file`); **85 human, by five people** — 71 by one manager on one day marking one rep's Zoom internal meetings (standups, coaching sessions, 1:1s, zero-length stubs; median 8 min) and 14 by four closers on their own calls. **At least eight of the 14 closer marks are real prospect conversations** — two graded CLOSED (78 and 65), follow-ups and losses of real prospects, no duplicates. H352's premise that a self-mark "cannot flatter" a rep is wrong for the close rate (removing a lost prospect raises it). Ruling needed before any classifier trains on them.
- **Justin's caveats, both present:** a 57-minute "Closer Sales Training (Mandatory)" reviewing a recorded prospect call sits unmarked, graded no-show 0 — one of **26 unmarked graded calls the grader itself calls internal in its summary** ("This recording is an internal …, not a prospect-facing sales call"), all 26 graded no-show, none graded as a sale, across 8 owners, one wearing a prospect-style title. And a closer marked a real 6-minute prospect reconnect not-a-sales-call — a human choosing the wrong side of caveat two.
- **Base rate:** 1,862 unmarked (1,631 graded: follow_up 1,104 · closed 287 · lost 145 · no_show 94). "Always say sales" scores ~98%. **Cost:** ~45,000 Sonnet tokens per graded call (grader + extractor + coaching); 12 marked and 26 internal calls each spent it. **At arrival:** title, duration, date, source, recorder, meeting id — no participants; the transcript is fetched inside `analyzeCall` before the grader, so a pre-read can answer before spend.
- **Placements:** A metadata gate (never a verdict — "Impromptu Zoom Meeting" is both a close and a team meeting) · B a small-model pre-read of the first ~5 minutes (~3k tokens) before the grader · C a structured `call_kind` field on the grader (free, after spend, and already 26/26 in prose with zero false positives among 1,631 graded sales). Recommended to Justin: B for spend, C for accuracy, agreement for the mark, everything else UNSURE and counting as today.
- **The bar, proposed:** the wrong NOT is the expensive error; auto-NOT precision ≥ 99% with zero real-prospect calls marked out in the held-out sample; auto-SALES no worse than today; ≤ 5% internal calls passing as sales; UNSURE reported as its own rate. **The blind harness** (Justin: "pulling a name out of a hat"): two shuffled sets with labels held aside, classify all then compare, tune on one and report only the other, three numbers beside the base rate, every wrong one shown in plain language. **The override guard** (`humanSaidItCounts`) covers the lift provided the new marker writes `not_sales_marked_by = null` and its own `exclusion_reason`. Nothing built.
- **Capture the reasoning (Justin's addition, 02:34):** the classifier states a reason CLASS (closed set) and one sentence at classify time, before the label; each run is a ROW per call (verdict, reason, prompt version, label at the time — accumulate, never overwrite); the human's reason is two fields beside the mark (today no mark carries one, so the harness collects them first). Mistakes are grouped by reason class; right-for-the-wrong-reason rows (reason class disagrees with the label's) are reported as their own table. **Does Fine Tune Coaching fit?** Yes for the LESSON (a team concept → a `coaching_correction` row with a new `given_on.surface`), no for the LABEL (a per-call fact → the mark). Substitution-not-suppression made concrete for a lane whose output IS a metric input: a team note may move a verdict toward SALES or UNSURE, never toward NOT; only the human mark removes a call. Grader and extractor never see the notes; the classifier is the only new reader.

### [H699] 🔎 BOOKED vs FOLLOW-UP AND OUTCOME ATTRIBUTION — RECON (2026-09-03). THE FOURTEEN CLOSER MARKS RE-READ, THE DATE THE 2026-08-03 RULING DOES NOT COVER, AND THE FIRST-NAME COLLISIONS UNDER THE MULTI-CALL PROSPECTS
- **Justin's ruling:** a reconnect is a follow-up, not a booked call, and must not count against a rep; the outcome belongs to the FIRST BOOKED CALL's date ("follow-up close") — an industry convention. The fourteen closer marks (H698) were the closers reaching for that flag with the only control they had; **13 of 14 have no earlier counted call for the prospect**, nine carry the calendar template — they are evidence of a missing flag, not training data, and are reversed only when the flag exists.
- **What 2026-08-03 gives:** within a window, one prospect = one denominator row and any close wins. **Not given:** the date — every surface windows by each call's date then groups, so a prospect spanning two windows is open in the first and closed in the second.
- **Measured:** 1,364 named prospects; 1,209 single-call (89%); 155 multi-call; 278 closes of which 45 on a later call (gap: 5 same-day, 17 in a week, 10 in a month, 13 over 30 days; 21 cross a month). **But 138 of the 155 multi-call prospects are one-word names and 70 of 83 titled one-word multi-call prospects carry 2+ different surnames** — different people under one first name ("Anthony" holds four closes for one rep, counted as one). Read pair by pair, ~14 of the 45 are genuine reconnects (~5% of closes); ~31 are strangers. The collisions already cost closes today: 201 closed calls on one-word prospects count as 195 closed prospects.
- **"Booked" is stored nowhere.** Template vs generic titles each have ~10% with an earlier call (a per-rep habit, not a signal); the title codes (PS, AF, IH, AP, AG, SM, H, DP, BW, HE, AJ, (LF)…) are unexplained — asked, not guessed; Zoom meeting ids are personal rooms (167 calls, 11 ids); **Fathom's transcript carries `matched_calendar_invitee_email` per speaker — an exact prospect identity received and dropped today** (coverage unmeasured; measuring it is a Fathom re-fetch). First-call-for-a-prospect depends on a grouping built from grader names that are **87% first-name-only**.
- **Justin: "for the names it's last names … it would have to be the content and context of the close, and the CRM plug-in."** Measured: 21% of first names (44% of people) collide team-wide; 8–35% per closer. The phrase test for references to an earlier call fires on 76% of later closes AND 78% of single-call closes — no discriminator; genuine pairs carry checkable facts ("the number I gave you last time was $750 per bed") that can CONFIRM a candidate, never choose among several. **Proposed scope: as far as transcripts allow now — link only on an exact signal or same closer + agreeing surname + close-in-time confirmed content, else unlinked — complete when the CRM lands.** A mislink is two wrong numbers; an unlinked follow-up is one honest one. **Order of the heavy lifts changes: names first** (surnames from the title, invitee email stored at arrival). H352 stays open; nothing built.

- **Justin's rulings that opened the block:** the title codes are calendar-name abbreviations (closed; none means rebook; never on a customer surface); names come first and attribution waits on them; this block stores and resolves nothing; new calls only; no token refresh to backfill; the linking policy is recorded verbatim in CLAUDE.md §4b before it is built; "extracting bad data is worse than no data" governs every part.

### [H701] 🔎 ZOOM CANNOT GIVE A PROSPECT'S EMAIL — VERIFIED, SCOPE SET (2026-09-03). THE DISPLAY-NAME CEILING, AND THE ORDER OF WORK BY SOURCE
- **Verified read-only, no refresh:** every stored Zoom token had expired ~2h earlier, so no live call was made — and none was needed: the stored `scope` on all four Zoom connections is `user:read:user` + `cloud_recording:read:*` (list recordings, files, recording, transcript). No `meeting:read`, no `report:read` — the participant endpoints are not callable by Scout's app at all. Zoom's own changelog: "Starting March 01, 2022 … if the participant is a guest, external, or an anonymous participant, you'll receive an empty value" for `user_email`; on 2023-03-03 Zoom removed `id` and `participant_user_id` for external participants — "Developers should now rely on the `registrant_id` field." Justin's research stands. One nuance: Zoom returns a guest's email when it "entered it during registration" OR "the host provided it through calendar integrations" — a second booking-flow route, still not a code change and still behind scopes Scout does not hold.
- **The Zoom display-name ceiling (204 Zoom calls with a transcript, 289 prospect-labelled speakers):** full name 184 (64%) · first name only 72 (25%) · device 20 · other 8 · phone number 3 · "Zoom user" 2. By call: 125 of 204 (61%) have a prospect-labelled speaker with a two-word-plus name; 23 have no prospect label; 58 have two or more prospect-labelled names (couples, co-hosts, the husband on the wife's account); 19 are one-speaker files. **61% is the ceiling, not the yield** — a display name is the account, not the speaker, and the linking policy takes it only as the second path.
- **The splitting pass, by rep (one-word prospects with 2+ disagreeing title surnames):** josh@scoutsystems.io 33 collisions / 84 calls / 6 closes swallowed · yazan 22 / 50 / 1 · joshua 7 / 15 · gabriel 6 / 15 · nick 2 / 4. **It is Fathom-only** — it needs the "| Name" title, and godwin.o's 13 one-word multi-call prospects are all Zoom, generic-titled, unresolvable by title (his 27 Zoom calls). Coverage on the three 062 columns: still zero rows — the cron had not run since 12:45Z at 15:36Z (past the observed 1h40–2h25 window); not a failure yet, noted.
- **Order of work, by reach:** coverage read (Fathom-only) → splitting pass (Fathom-only) → linking (Fathom first path; Zoom second path only) → follow-up flag and attribution (both sources, on whatever is linked) → the three-state classifier (both sources; the transcript is the input). Registration/calendar-integration filed under the CRM row. Nothing built.

### [H717] 🔎 A BUYING SIGNAL IS AN EFFECT (2026-09-03). THE CORPUS STORES 1,050 EFFECTS AND ALMOST NO CAUSES; THE CAUSES ARE IN THE STORED TRANSCRIPTS; A FIELD, NOT A LONGER CHUNK
- **Justin's reframe:** "there's context behind a buying signal — not just what the prospect said, but what led up to that." The move that produced it is the coachable part.
- **Measured:** of 1,050 harvested buying signals, 858 have an earlier harvested moment on the same call, 511 an earlier CLOSER moment, **133 a closer moment within three minutes** (78 against every highlight the extractor kept); median gap ~3.5 min harvested, ~5 min all highlights. The extractor keeps almost no closer lines as moments (closer speaks on 55 of 2,775 buying-signal highlights, 0 of 1,512 objections). **The "what happened" sentence names a cause on 39 of 1,050** (prose: "after the closer painted the vision…", "after the closer reframed the entry cost…") — thrown away as text; 176 describe only the effect. **The transcript window before every one of the 1,050 is stored** (264 calls, per-turn timestamps): ~12 chars/s → three minutes ≈ 2,200 chars ≈ 550 tokens, no fetch.
- **Recoverable both ways:** backward pass ≈ 1,050 × (550 window + 400 prompt + 80 out) ≈ 1.0M in / 0.08M out → **≈ $4.30 Sonnet / ≈ $1.40 Haiku** (five-minute window ≈ $6); forward: a field on the extractor at write time, no extra read, version bump, new calls only. Neither before the vocabulary of moves exists — free-prose causes are 1,050 more sentences searchable by nothing.
- **The structural read:** the single quote is the wrong unit for a buying signal; the coachable thing is the SEQUENCE (closer did → prospect said → what happened next). The product already has the after-shape (objections: closer_response on 1,487 of 1,512; the coaching lane renders quote → response → outcome) and NOTHING for the before. **A harvested moment should carry its preceding move as a FIELD** (closer line, its timestamp, the move name; the embedded text gains a short clause and stays ~400 chars) — never a longer chunk, which is the 3,100-char winning-call defect in a new place.
- **"Why you closed the deals you did" is unanswerable from effects without causes**; the "you've done it before" coaching needs the cause. The 287 closed calls have their signals harvested, their moves unrecorded, their transcripts stored. Nothing built; order: the vocabulary → the extractor field → the ≈$4 backward pass → the coaching lane can say what a rep did.

### [H718] 🔎 THE CAPTURE OF CAUSES — DESIGNED, COSTED, NOT BUILT (2026-09-03). THE VOCABULARY APPROVED; THE ARC IS THE UNIT; TWO OR THREE LOCATED LINES OR NO MOVE; `none` IS A FEATURE; THE CALLBACK NEEDS BOTH ENDS
- **The vocabulary (closed, sixteen moves) is in CLAUDE.md §4b.** Free prose produces 400 phrasings of one thing; the closed set is the point.
- **The arc, measured:** on 970 signals with a readable window, two+ closer questions within 3 min for 807 (83%), 5 min 913 (94%), 8 min 949 (98%); 11 had no closer question in 8 min; the first question inside a 10-minute window sits at the window's edge (median 550 s back), i.e. closer questions are continuous and NO RULE finds where a thread began — a model reading the window can. v1: five minutes, widened once to eight, then `none`.
- **The field:** `cause { move | none, none_reason (arrived_pre_sold | no_closer_work | not_evidenced), evidence [2–3 verbatim CLOSER lines with timestamps, each located by lib/quote-locate.js or the whole cause refused], arc_start_seconds, signal {highlight_id, ts, quote}, summary (framework voice, from the evidence only) }` on the highlight and mirrored to the harvested moment's metadata; the embedded text gains the move and the summary and stays ~400 chars — a field, never a longer chunk.
- **`none` as a feature:** 56 of 1,050 signals read as pre-sold in their own sentence (research, notes, a target city); the closer earns nothing there; the per-rep `none` count is the second most useful thing a manager can be told.
- **The third tier (let it slide · dug deeper · banked it and used it later):** needs both ends; the moment set holds both ends on 141 of 326 calls and almost never the callback line itself (46 sentences say "earlier", none an explicit callback). Field `disclosure_handling { tier, disclosure, response, callback }` with the same guard. Forward: free at write time (the extractor reads the whole transcript). Backward: the 264 calls behind the signals are 4.1M transcript tokens.
- **Cost at list:** cause backward pass ≈ $7.50 Sonnet / $2.30 Haiku at five minutes (≈ $9.20 / $3.10 at eight); callback backward ≈ $14 / $4.70; forward both fields ≈ 1.5¢ more per call (the extractor cap 3,000 → ~4,000; measure the six longest calls first); re-embed ≈ one cent. Recommended: both fields at write time in one bump; the two backward passes as two separate approvals, the callback second, after the first pass's `none` rate is seen. Nothing runs.

Each signal pairs at most once; DQs in order.
- **What "ignored or deflected" is derived from:** the extractor's v8a `handling` field, written at analysis time on risk_signal/barrier rows only (the test: did the closer engage with the SUBSTANCE, or acknowledge and move on; warmth is not engagement). NULL (pre-v8a) never pairs — absence is not a verdict. On the live pairs `deflected` is 92 of 103 — the model's generous label; in the pairs that stood by hand the deflection was real ("I'm not a salesperson", "that's fine, nothing set aside, okay"). The signal end is speaker-verified on 98 of 103.
- **Unfloored: 103 pairs on 69 of 117 DQ calls; gap median 380 s, 26 under two minutes, 47 under five, 63 under ten.** Sections: discovery→close 29, discovery→discovery 22, intro→discovery 13, close→close 12.
- **TEN READ BY HAND (seeded draw, `~/Desktop/scan-reports/missed-signal/hand-read-ten.txt`): 3 stand clearly, 1 partially, 6 do not.** The three that stand: a prior bad investment deflected at 3:03 → "even 20 grand, I don't have it" at 39:48 (36 min — Justin's exact shape, with "living paycheck to paycheck" in the DQ's own observation); "right now, none" set aside, waved past with "that's fine, okay" at 12:11 → "my debt is too high" at 29:09 (16 min); "I'm a realtor too" ignored at 0:28 → "mostly just the certification, I know the real estate" at 10:10 (9 min, a no-need DQ). The partial: a frustrated arrival deflected → "already past that stage" 20 min later — a flag deflected, then a DQ, but the flag does not foreshadow THAT DQ. **The six that fail are ALL under three minutes or the closer acting**: the DQ surfacing across consecutive answers (maxed cards → "maybe a couple grand", 26 s; a medical disclosure → wants roommates, 27 s), a refusal to share income two minutes before a no-need statement the closer then probed, a shallow-research flag 1:41 before a cash figure, and TWICE the closer disqualifying the prospect himself within three minutes of the flag ("our conversation's a little premature") — that is the behaviour being coached TOWARDS, not a miss.
- **The shape, therefore:** a FIVE-MINUTE FLOOR (`MIN_GAP_SECONDS = 300`: every drawn pair under three minutes failed, every pair over nine stood; ten minutes would also hold — 42 pairs on 33 calls — the five is the looser cut pending a bigger read), and a DQ the CLOSER speaks is excluded (8 of 71 DQ rows in the unfloored pairs). **At the floor with the exclusion: 51 pairs on 39 calls** (rep 8d9dfc8c 20 on 16, a99f548b 11 on 6, Josh 6 on 6, the rest 1–5). A rate is not a finding; the shape is: the pair is the same move as tying back in, inverted — one vocabulary, two outcomes.

Measured on stored rows, a bar of "a moment needs a reason to exist" — coachable: missed_opportunity · objection partial/unhandled · risk/barrier ignored/deflected; applaudable: verified closer strong_moment · objection handled · risk/barrier addressed · buying signal with an evidenced move — keeps 4.24 per call (median 4) against 6.14 today; 426 of 1,561 calls fall to three or fewer; 8 calls to zero. **What it removes: 2,517 buying signals with no evidenced move (the largest single class — a prospect line that credits the closer with nothing), 170 rapport moments, 145 unverified strong moments, 138 lone DQ signals.** **What it costs:** at write time NOTHING new — every field the bar reads the extractor already emits; the change is a prompt rule plus a filter and a version bump. Backward, the filter is free on every leg but one: "buying signal with an evidenced move" is known on 726 signals only; assessing the other ~2,050 is ≈ $21 at 1.03¢ each — not proposed, stated so the cost of knowing is on record. ### [H721] 🔧 THE SELECTIVITY BAR — SHIPPED FORWARD ONLY (v42, 2026-09-04): A MOMENT NEEDS A REASON TO EXIST. THREE REAL CALLS SIDE BY SIDE; THE 36-MINUTE PAIR RENDERED

(2) Wire the pair in two places — the review page beside the moment, and the coaching page for managers to see — ONE renderer, two placements; the sentence stays assembled in code, no principle, no model call, no coaching voice; the floor and the closer-DQ exclusion hold. (3) **THE CORRECTION THAT CHANGES WHAT THE PAIR IS:** *"Even though the prospect trying and failing doesn't exactly line up with a financial DQ, it IS a fear signal that should've been resolved and uncovered."* The flag and the disqualification need not be the same kind of thing; the pair is valid because the flag went unexplored, not because it predicted that outcome. So the sentence must NOT say "foreshadowed" — the honest claim is: a signal was raised, it was not explored, and the call later ended in a disqualification. It connects to the three-way boundary on file: hesitant about money regardless of excuse is FEAR; genuinely cannot afford it is a financial DQ; a fear signal left unexplored is how a call reaches the close before anyone knows which.
- **The sentence now:** `At 00:03:03 the prospect said "…". The closer replied "…" and moved on. The signal was not explored. 36 min later, at 00:39:48, the prospect said "…" — a disqualification.` Pinned: no "foreshadow", "caused", "led to", "because".

### [H724] 🔎🔧 FOLD MISSED SIGNALS INTO COACHABLE MOMENTS (ruled; the ranking reported, not built) · NO UNEARNED QUOTES — THE EVIDENCE SUBJECT CHECK (built) · "THE PROSPECT LEFT" GETS ITS OWN TYPE (ruled; shape reported) (2026-09-04)
- **CLAUDE BUILT A FEATURE OUT OF A LESSON — the second time this session.** Justin: *"The reason we were talking about closers missing signals was to help you understand the sales process and what context makes a good or bad moment — and how tying things back helps and missing things hurts. I'd prefer a coachable moments section that includes moments like this WHEN NEEDED."* The first instance was the arc capture's panel-shaped thinking around the vocabulary of moves (H718–H719). RULE: when Justin explains sales logic, the deliverable is the DESIGN being right, not a surface named after the lesson. A manager does not want a panel of one defect type; they want what is worth their attention on this call, and a missed signal is ONE KIND of that. The pair logic, the five-minute floor and the closer-DQ exclusion survive; only the placement changes.
- **THE RANKING RULE, PROPOSED (not built — Justin rules):** measured on the team's 30-day window (830 counted real calls) the bar keeps 1,600 coachable moments — deflected risk signals 476, missed opportunities 422, objections left partial 335, unhandled 219, ignored signals 68, deflected barriers 66, ignored barriers 14 — plus 26 pairs. A panel that lists by kind is 30% deflected signals and 26 pairs at the bottom. **The rule: a coachable moment earns a place by its CONSEQUENCE on the same call, and one kind cannot fill the panel.** Tier 1: the missed-signal pair (a flag unexplored, a disqualification later; 26, 18 of which stood by hand). Tier 2: an objection left unhandled on a call that did not close (219 on 159 calls; none on a closed call — the last objection before the loss). Tier 3: a missed opportunity on a call that did not close (395 on 301 calls). Deflected and ignored signals earn a place ONLY inside a pair (unpaired they are 545 in the window and "deflected" is the extractor's generous label). Caps: one moment per call, three per rep, newest first — so Godwin's 11 pairs cannot be the panel. Predicted mix under the caps for this team (8 reps → at most 24 items): pairs ≈ a quarter, unhandled objections ≈ half, missed opportunities ≈ a quarter — the prediction to check against the first render. Each item carries its consequence in code ("the call did not close" / "N min later, a disqualification"), never a coaching sentence. The review-page duplication went with it: beside a moment the block shows only the gap and the disqualification end (BUILT, `missedPairHtml` inline; test).
- **NO UNEARNED QUOTES — BUILT (lane v9):** Justin: *"some of the quotes Scout pulls and the context don't make sense… less quotes, more summary/coaching."* Not fewer quotes — no quote that does not prove the claim it sits under; a claim built on counts stands alone. THE LIVE DEFECT: "partner objections handled 5 of 177, surfaced too late, Nathan and Nick" carried a prospect saying they feel comfortable buying. `evidenceMismatch` checks WHOSE quote (Nick was named → passed); nothing checked WHAT it was about. **What a subject check is built from:** the moment's stored `type`, `objection_category` and `section` — exact, no model call. The lane now asks for `subject {kind, category, section}` per insight (kinds = the eight moment types + `section` + `count`), tags each candidate with type/category/section in the prompt, and `evidenceSubjectMismatch(subject, ev)` drops the quote when the cited moment's stored fields disagree, when the kind is `count` (no quote by design), or when no checkable subject was declared (absent beats wrong). The claim and its counts stand; the card already renders a quoteless insight cleanly. `resolveInsights` is module-level and EXECUTED by `test/evidence-subject.test.js` with the live defect planted; the older rep-binding pin was re-anchored and now executes too. **Does it cover it?** It covers every claim whose subject is a moment kind, an objection category or a section — the kinds the lane is asked to produce. It cannot check a claim about a metric that is not a moment (a rate, a duration) except by refusing it a quote, which is the ruling. It does not check that the quote's WORDS support the claim within the right kind (a partner objection cited for a claim about partner objections surfacing "too late" is the right kind; whether it shows lateness is a reading the check does not make) — that residue is a hand read, not a rule.
- **"THE PROSPECT LEFT" — RULED, SHAPE REPORTED, NOT BUILT.** Six of the eight failed pairs ended on the prospect leaving (reschedule, hang-up after a confrontation, withdrawal) typed `disqualify_signal`. The shape: a ninth highlight type `prospect_left` — the prospect ends, defers or withdraws from the call without a stated reason the offer does not apply; prompt text (v43) with the discriminator (a REASON the offer does not apply = DQ; leaving without one = left); `VALID_HIGHLIGHT_TYPES` + `PROSPECT_POSITION_TYPES`; the CHECK constraint (`call_highlights_type_check`, migration 038's list) widened by a migration BEFORE deploy; the dashboard's type label and the KB/harvest group tables; `evidence-rule` NEGATIVE_TYPES; the pair excludes it as a DQ end (a leaving is its own end, unpaired for now); the bar lets a lone exit fall as a lone DQ does. **WHAT MOVES: NO RATE.** `disqualify_signal` moments are read by no close rate, no DQ count and no denominator — the DQ OUTCOME is manual-only (`lib/dq-exclusion.js isDisqualified` reads `outcome = 'disqualified'`); the moment type is read only by the pairs route, the moment bar, the evidence rule, the performance synthesis's loss class and the catalog's descriptive count. So no live board number moves; what changes is the DQ-moment count itself (138 stored, of which a text heuristic marks 10 and the hand read 6 of 26 as leaving) and every pair's end. Before/after therefore = the weekly count of DQ moments and of `prospect_left` moments from v43 on; history unchanged (new calls only). Not built until Justin says.
- **Filed for the end of the session, not now:** rep-card sort on the team page; "Godwin Ona's Personal Meeting Room" rendering where a prospect name belongs on every surface that shows a raw title.

TEAM RECOMMENDATIONS — selling context (SYNTHESIS categories, +winning_call: 2,911 chars of Josh's calls) + corrections. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY — selling context + corrections. OBJECTIONS SUMMARY — corrections (and selling context via its lane). THE OBJECTIONS WHY (`why-prose`) — nothing. - **THE FOUR-STEP PLAN, costed from the findings:** ① MECHANICAL EVIDENCE CHECK — section and category stored on every moment; built for the recommendations lane (v9 subject + v10 bar); extending it to the other citing lanes (objections summary, performance summary, needs-work evidence, digest) is code and a version bump per lane; zero model cost; each lane regenerates once per team on its next load. ② LANES MUST NOT CONTRADICT — Justin's correction recorded: generalising about "the team" is FINE; the defect is two lanes asserting opposites on one page because each is generated blind. Pages that carry two or more generated lanes: Team → Coaching (recommendations beside the deterministic Coachable Moments), Objections (why-prose + summary), Performance (summary + cards). Cost: a shared "page facts" block (the deterministic numbers and the coachable list) handed to every synthesis on that page + a post-check that a claim's direction agrees with the facts — no extra model call, ~1–2k tokens more per call; or one synthesis per page (a larger change). ③ THE REP'S HISTORY — stored today per rep: per-moment coaching text (v30+), `one_thing` per call, cached syntheses with dates, corrections. "Coached on partner objections three times and it has not moved" is COMPUTABLE from stored rows (objection_category + resolution over time per rep, plus prior coaching moments by category) — deterministic, then prompt lines; tokens only. ④ JUDGEMENT — depends on the KB holding Justin's method and THE OFFER; today the team's offer is absent and the method lives only hand-typed in prompts (H715); the prerequisite is the offer, the qualifications and the script ON FILE for the team and READ for the reps.

Guard `test/doctrine-invisible.test.js` (the predicate on a doctrine row for four scopes with a non-vacuous control; the migration's conjunct pinned as text and position; the lanes' eleven on a fake wire).
- **ITEM 2 — WHAT FEEDS THE LINE, enumerated before the prompt.** Per rep the panel holds up to five items (H726: one per call, three cost + two forward, tier before recency), each carrying: kind and direction; the prospect's line with its timestamp and section; the closer's reply ONLY where proven (`provenCloserResponse`); the extractor's observation; handling and resolution; for a missed-signal pair BOTH ends and the gap; for an earned buying signal the arc MOVE and its summary (v41); the call's date and outcome. NOT used: the disclosure tier (`disclosure_handling` is written on prospect moments the panel does not select), the objection category on non-objection kinds, the bar reason, anything about the prospect beyond the quoted lines. The outcome reaches the model through `outcomeForAdvice` (H733): a call carrying a DQ is "Disqualified (the prospect could not buy — not a lost deal, not a failed close)".
- **THE DESIGN.** `lib/rep-line.js`: one model call per rep per period (lane `rep-line`, Sonnet, 400 out), the prompt = the rep's items by id + team material + manager notes + the doctrine block (`LANE_KEYS['rep-line']`, nine units), and the SHAPE as a framework — "<N> calls where they <did the thing> and <what it cost or won>" — with the rules stated as things checked in code. The model returns `{kind: pattern|strength|none, judgement, evidence_ids, calls_claimed}`; the NAME AND THE DASH ARE ADDED IN CODE (the first name, Justin's shape; the board name — "Josh N", "Josh P" — where two reps share a first name, so two rows never read the same). Cached in `objection_synthesis_cache` (`rep_line`, snapped window, hash = the items' ids and outcomes + the version + `kbHash`); the material loaded ONCE per team before any line (H731 — nothing on file → no model call, the one shape on the payload); at most six calls in flight (H250); a hung call is `unavailable` after 60 s and NOT cached, so the next load retries — the first live pass hung on one call for ten minutes before that guard existed. The route reads ONE gather, `lib/coachable-team.js loadCoachableTeam`, shared with the measurement script — what is priced is what is sent.
- **THE GUARD IS CODE — `verifyLine`, every rule executed in `test/rep-line.test.js`:** every cited id must be beneath the line (a plant that removes or discards that check fails a case where the COUNT would otherwise pass — the first plant passed because a ghost id also broke the count, a vacuous guard, fixed in the same hour); a number in the judgement (digits or one..ten/both) must equal the distinct calls cited and `calls_claimed` must agree; a pattern needs two calls (one call is a restatement); no quoted line (a word track); never the prospect's name — PROPER-NOUN tokens of the cited items' `prospect_name`, case-sensitive, placeholders ("Prospect", "Unknown prospect", the calendar stand-ins) never counted; never the closer's own name; no "but/however/though" after a number and none at all on a strength (never diminishing); a DQ call among the evidence never framed as a loss (`framesDqAsLoss`); never out of isolating; ≤34 words. A failing line is REFUSED — the row reads "Scout could not anchor a pattern to these moments this period." — and the model's raw answer is kept on the cache record (never rendered) so a refusal can be READ, not guessed. `none` → "no pattern this period across N moments"; no items → why (no counted calls vs nothing qualifying). The route executed on a fake wire with the seam stubbed: the line attached to the rep, its evidence beneath it, its count matching, the cache written, a ghost id refused FOR THAT REASON, nothing on file → no model call. The page's renderer executed from the live source: one collapsed row per rep, the line as the head, the cited moments first with the "Evidence for the line" mark, `aria-expanded` driven by `state.repLineOpen` (resets on pivot).

### [H735] 🔧 STEP 3 — THE REP'S HISTORY REACHES THE COACHING: THE SMALLEST RECORD, THE COUNT ON THE LINE, THE BAR FOR "NOT MOVED" (2026-09-05)
- **§1 THE ENUMERATION, by execution against the live tables (what Scout persists about what it has told a rep).** (a) **Coaching entries per call** — `call_highlights.coaching` (+ `coaching_applied_notes`): 653 entries on 183 calls for 9 reps, earliest 2026-08-25 (v30), latest today; grain = one text per moment; **deleted on a re-grade** (`persistHighlights` inserts the new set then deletes the old ids — the text goes with them); a prompt version bump leaves them (new calls only); keyed to NO pattern — the moment's type, category, resolution and handling sit beside the text. (b) **Per-closer syntheses** (`objection_synthesis_cache`: objections 43, performance 84, why_prose 306, needs_work 240, coaching_areas 2…) — keyed by user × window × set-hash; a row is REGENERATED when the set changes and the old rows linger by hash, but none says which pattern was coached on which call; not a history. (c) **Recommendations** (team 175, team_objections 53, team_needs_work 107) — same shape, per team. (d) **The digest** (99 rows, since 07-22) — per manager per day, by date; prose about the day, no per-rep pattern. (e) **The panel moments and their kinds** — computed on every load from the highlights; NOTHING persisted. (f) **The rep line** (37 rows today) — cached by window and hash; its evidence ids are POSITIONAL (m1…m5), not call ids; regenerated when the set moves; no history. (g) Manager corrections: 2 rows, a record of the manager's interventions, not of Scout's. (h) `model_usage` lane `coaching`: that coaching was written for a call, with no content. **THE FINDING: everything is regenerated except the per-moment text on the highlight, which is deleted on re-grade and keyed to no pattern. Scout could not tell the first time from the fourth. The block became creating the record.**
- **THE RECORD — the smallest that answers "which rep, which pattern, when, on which call":** `coaching_history` (migration 073): `user_id, team_key, pattern_key, fathom_call_id, highlight_id, call_date, surface, version`, UNIQUE (rep, pattern, call). The pattern key is CODE over stored fields — `objection:<category>` for an objection left unhandled/partial, `missed_signal` for a risk signal or barrier ignored/deflected, `missed_opportunity`; handled objections, addressed signals, disqualifications and leavings count as nothing (`patternKey`). Written by the coaching pass with each entry it writes (idempotent); **built once from the entries on file: 653 entries → 335 rows (missed_signal 106, missed_opportunity 101, fear 54, partner 42, timing 27, logistical 5), 9 reps, 162 calls** (`scripts/coaching-history-backfill-2026-09-05.js`, dry then apply, data only). A re-grade reissues highlight ids; the call and the pattern stay.
- **§2 THE TWO CLAIMS.** "Scout has coached this on N calls this period" = distinct calls in the record for that rep and that pattern inside the panel's window; it earns a place on a PATTERN line from the third call (`REPEAT_FLOOR` 3 — "third time this period" changes what a manager does; "once before" does not), never on a strength. **"And the handle rate has not moved" — THE BAR, for Justin to rule (`movedAssessment`, pure, executed through its cases):** measurable only for an objection category (the strict handle rate, `isHandled` + `countsAsObjection`, the same definition every surface reads); BEFORE = the rep's objections of that category before the record's first coaching of it, SINCE = after; **each window ≥ `MIN_BUCKET` (6) attempts** — the one comparison floor already ruled for the rep-card arrows (H704), reused rather than a second floor; **headroom: the before rate ≤ 80%**, so a 20-point rise was possible; **moved = the since rate is at least 20 points above the before rate** (with six attempts one more handled objection is ~17 points — one objection alone is noise); **not moved = cleared and under 20**. Under the bar Scout says the count and stops; "not enough data" is never rendered as "no improvement". Live today: NO rep clears it — Nathan's partner objections, the only objection-category pattern line, fail on "fewer than 6 attempts in a window" — so every clause is the count alone. The pattern keys `missed_signal` and `missed_opportunity` carry no rate and never get a movement claim.
- **§3 WHERE IT SURFACES.** The rep line: the route (`GET /team/coachable-moments`) reads the record for the board inside the window, keys each PATTERN line by the most frequent key among its cited items (`repLinePatternKey`), and attaches `history {key, calls, window, assessment}` + `history_clause` in CODE; the page appends the clause after the line as a quieter span. The coaching pass: the record for this rep (all time) is read before the prompt; for each of the call's moments whose pattern Scout has coached on ≥ 2 earlier calls, one HISTORY line ("partner objections: coached on 6 earlier calls (most recent …)") with the rule — coach the repeat at its CAUSE, never a word track, NEVER AN ACCUSATION, the count only where it changes the advice; the words record/history/log never to the closer (the first measured after-text wrote "belongs in the record now" — fixed before commit). `scoldsRepeat` drops "yet again", "you keep", "same mistake", "for the Nth time"… in code before the write. The record is written after each entry with the entry (`recordCoaching`). v47.
- **§4 PROVEN BY LOOKING.** The lines, live, via the page's own query (window 2026-08-07 → today), every one a cache hit (no spend): Godwin (pattern, missed signal) — "Scout has coached this on 6 calls this period."; Nathan (pattern, partner objections) — "…on 6 calls this period." ### [H736] 🔧 A REP WITH NO COACHING ENTRIES — THE CONDITION SET, BY CAPABILITY; THE COACHING PASS LEAVES A MARK. THE REP-CARD SORT RULED (2026-09-05)
- **ITEM 1 — THE CONDITION SET, enumerated across every rep and call, not by looking at Josh N.** A graded call produces zero coaching entries when ANY of: (1) it was graded at a prompt version below v30 (2026-08-29), before the coaching pass existed — new calls only, never mass re-analysed; (2) it is marked not a sales call (the pass is gated on the flag); (3) the pass ran and returned before the model — `read_failed`, `no_coachable_moments`, `no_material` (since H731), `unparseable`, or an exception; (4) the pass, which is fire-and-forget by design (the drain dies on a redeploy, nothing optional may lengthen the window), was KILLED WITH THE PROCESS after the call was already marked done; (5) on a RE-GRADE, `persistHighlights` deletes the old highlights and their coaching text with them, and the second run's pass then fell into (3) or (4). Executed over every done call (synthetic and excluded rows out): **1,721 graded calls; 214 at v30 or later; 187 of those with coachable moments; 183 coached; FOUR uncoached** — Dre Wisam 1 (2026-08-30 15:52Z, v33), Nick O'Neal 3 (2026-09-01 16:36–16:37Z, v37, one batch); plus one call outside the counted set (marked not a sales call, correctly skipped). **Josh N (Josh Niebloom): 16 graded calls, EVERY one at v26–v29, the last graded 2026-08-29 — condition (1), not a failure: no call of his has been graded since the pass shipped.** No trace of a rep on any team who is graded at v30+ and uncoached beyond those four.
- **Which failure, executed:** `model_usage` (logging from 2026-08-31) shows two of Nick's three had a coaching model call on their FIRST grade (2026-08-31 23:47Z; 2026-09-03 17:47Z) and were RE-GRADED (2026-09-01 16:36Z; 2026-09-03 19:27Z) with NO coaching call after — **coached, then lost on the re-grade, and never re-coached.** The third (6a2e7d80) had one grade and no coaching call ever; Dre's predates logging. The three Nick calls at 16:36–16:37Z sit inside the swap window of the 16:29Z push (2eda78b) — consistent with (4), the pass dying with the old process; the 09-03 19:27Z and 08-30 15:52Z cases coincide with no push (NOT VERIFIED which of (3)/(4) they were — the logs have rotated). One grading path exists (`analyzeCall`) and it always reaches the pass; no path re-grades without it.

### [H740] Coaching context without invented causation — 2026-09-05
Justin approved the corrective block with `c` after the eight-call recovery pilot produced five no-change responses and six withheld drafts. H413 requires a reader to understand what happened and how the call ended; the old implementation demanded a cause and cost even while forbidding unsupported causation. That unconditional requirement is superseded: describe the recorded outcome and observed continuation, and leave causal impact unknown when the evidence does not establish it. A general method is not evidence of what caused this particular call outcome. Missing stored reply data does not establish silence. The reviewer must distinguish missing isolation from criticism of correct isolation, and upstream financial qualification from trying to overcome genuine inability to buy. A directional request for information is not by itself a word track.
Built locally as analysis v50 / evidence review v3; old approved v1/v2 reviews remain readable without upgrading provenance. Four regression tests failed before the correction; the full 2,493-test suite and six saved-response gate replays pass. These checks do not establish new model efficacy. No new paid output was generated and nothing from this correction was deployed. A four-call real-output test is prepared but requires fresh spending approval, followed by Justin reading its output before deployment.

Justin: "moving forward you only need to ask permission is something is going to cost over $20" followed by "send it". This supersedes H058's approval-before-any-spend requirement. ### [H746] Manager priorities and named evidence examples — 2026-09-05
This is the next build, ahead of broad historical coaching recovery. The live individual-call writer stays useful; the manager presentation changes. Supersedes the manager-only presentation of “One thing to do differently” as the primary content. Personal Call Review coaching remains second-person advice.

1. **In progress — wording:** use “the call ended” for termination. Reserve “closed” for won deals; never “the call closed open.” Enforce in generated coaching without modifying verbatim transcript quotes or changing outcome definitions.
2. **In progress — trustworthy grouping contract:** group validated examples by a specific coaching issue, deduplicate calls, apply the selected team/closer/date scope, and separate assessed calls from unassessed calls. A positive example or a generic Discovery section cannot prove a missing-follow-up pattern. Never infer “3 of 8” from one excerpt or treat unassessed calls as negatives.
3. **Next — issue assessment:** identify the specific issue from complete relevant exchanges plus endings and team guidance; preserve evidence and distinguish unresolved objections from legitimate barriers. Verify the issue and every stated qualifier before counting it. Existing broad section labels and free-text advice are insufficient. Measure a bounded real-call trial before any historical processing.
4. **Next — manager presentation:** Coaching priority → verified frequency and explicit period → example with prospect name, closer name, factual continuation/recorded outcome and Watch clip. No separate Manager action block. Individual-call advice may illustrate the priority, never substitute for the pattern summary.
